## Pediatric bronchoscopy {#pediatric-bronchoscopy}

**Partnerships for Global Surgery · Sponsored engineering project · 2026–present**

A pediatric rigid bronchoscope should remain usable and durable in hospitals with very different resources. I’m working with a seven-person Clinic team and clinical advisors on an affordable system that integrates a rigid tube, handle, distal-camera endoscope, forceps, and suction. My contributions include miniature-camera selection and integration, handle ideation, camera-cleaning prototypes, and thermal testing. The current concept uses a **2.0 mm camera**, a **5.7 mm outer-diameter bronchoscope**, and a **720 × 720, 30 fps** video feed.

*Current stage:* Work in progress—requirements development, detailed design, and preliminary prototype evaluation. Manufacturing, simulated-use testing, iteration, and broader validation remain ahead.

[Read the full bronchoscope project →](pediatric-bronchoscope.qmd){.text-link}

## Autonomous underwater robot {#autonomous-underwater-robot}

**Experimental Engineering · 2026**

Our four-person team built an AUV for depth-resolved environmental sensing at Dana Point. I designed analog signal-conditioning circuits for pressure, thermistor, pH, and relative-light measurements; supported waterproof mechanical integration; and used calibration and live serial data to debug the system. The final deployment reached **2.61 ± 0.05 m**, captured cooling and reduced light with depth, and exposed why the pH channel needs seawater-specific calibration.

[Read the full AUV project →](autonomous-underwater-robot.qmd){.text-link}

## MuddSub AUV electronics {#muddsub-electronics}

**PCB Team Member · 2026–present**

Contribute to PCB design and verification for MuddSub's eight-thruster autonomous underwater vehicle. The team's Rev. 1 electrical stack separates power distribution from real-time signal control: a power board generates **12 V, 5 V, and 3.3 V rails**, while a Teensy 4.1 signal board handles thruster PWM and embedded interfaces. I also contribute to waterproof packaging, buoyancy, chassis integration, and serviceability.

[Read the full MuddSub project →](muddsub.qmd){.text-link} · [Visit MuddSub](https://muddsub.org/){.text-link}

## Filament waste collection {#filament-waste-collection}

**Engineering Design and Manufacturing · 2025**

Worked with the Harvey Mudd Makerspace on a collection system for the 3D-printing lab. Our five-person team prototyped a perimeter track and chute interface using CAD, 3D printing, laser cutting, and machining. Steward trials on a six-printer prototype surfaced the next mechanical changes: tighter track tolerance and a lighter, stiffer drive system. A related disposal workflow reduced manual disposal time by approximately **50%** according to the resume project record.

## Multicycle RISC-V processor {#multicycle-risc-v-processor}

**Computer Engineering · 2025**

Implemented a hierarchical 32-bit RISC-V processor in SystemVerilog with a controller, datapath, ALU, register file, immediate generator, finite-state machine, and unified memory. The processor reuses its ALU and memory across multiple cycles and supports arithmetic, loads, stores, branches, jumps, and `AUIPC`. Program-level simulation ended with the expected write of **`0x1067` to address 84**.

[Read the full processor project →](multicycle-processor.qmd){.text-link}

## Laser tag system {#laser-tag-system}

**Microprocessors project · 2026 · in progress**

Developing an infrared laser-tag game with two blasters and two vests. The system concept combines hit detection and three-life game logic, sound and LED feedback, and an ESP8266-based local scoreboard. The hardware architecture combines an STM32 MCU, FPGA, and a custom PCB; implementation and game testing are ongoing.

[Code and PCB repository](https://github.com/bphung-01/Laser_Tag_Code_PCB)
